name: Proactive grant review (client message → team channel)

data.label: Skip unless the channel is bound to a client entity

inputMapping.prompt: You detect when a grants-agency CLIENT is asking US to review their work on a Stellar Community Fund grant. ANY message where the client says a deliverable is ready, done, finished, or submitted, OR explicitly asks for our review/feedback = reviewNeeded TRUE (e.g. 'finished the abstract', 'ready for your review', 'submitted section X', 'can you check this'). Casual chat, questions, scheduling, or logistics = reviewNeeded FALSE. Respond with ONLY a JSON object: {"reviewNeeded": boolean, "milestone": string (short label like 'abstract' / 'build dossier', empty if false), "reason": string}. Client message: {{trigger.payload.data.content}}

data.label: Only continue if a review is actually needed
Resolve the client's TEAM channel (FIREWALL: never the client channel)
Flag it on the TEAM channel (FIREWALL: never the client channel)
Find the client's grant_submission via the graph (submitted_by, inbound)
Run the Stellar grant advisor on the resolved dossier

inputMapping.prompt: You are the stellar-scf-grants-advisor: an expert reviewer of Stellar Community Fund (SCF) grant submissions. Apply the SCF methodology (clear problem/solution fit, measurable milestones, realistic budget, Stellar-ecosystem alignment, traction evidence) to pre-review the client's milestone BEFORE the human reviewer. Milestone: {{steps.detect.output.milestone}}. Client message: {{trigger.payload.data.content}}. Grant submission relations (graph edges to the client's grant_submission entity): {{steps.resolve-dossier.output.relations}}. Produce a concise, actionable pre-review (strengths, gaps, concrete fixes, and a go / needs-work call). Respond with ONLY a JSON object: {"summary": string}.

data.label: Post the AI review to the TEAM channel
Only persist an analysis + advance when a grant_submission is linked
Persist the pre-review as a durable analysis entity
Link the analysis to the submission (analyzes)
Advance the submission status to in-review (a review is now underway)

metadata.purpose: PROACTIVE: when a client posts a milestone in their comms channel ('finished abstract', 'needs review'), the AI detects it, pre-reviews the grant with the Stellar advisor skill, and surfaces BOTH the flag and the review on the TEAM channel — so nobody has to launch an agent. It then PERSISTS the pre-review as a durable `analysis` entity linked to the client's `grant_submission` (analyzes) and advances the submission's `status` to `in-review`, so the pipeline reflects that a review is underway — not just an ephemeral message. The automation holds NO channel id: it resolves the client's team channel from the bound client entity at runtime via channel.resolve, and finds the submission via graph.relations(submitted_by, inbound). FIREWALL: all AI output goes to the resolved TEAM channel, NEVER the client-comms source channel; the analysis/advance writes are governed (proposal or auto-approve).
prerequisites: FIREWALL (non-negotiable): both output nodes post to {{steps.resolve-team.output.channelId}} — the TEAM channel resolved by the `resolve-team` capability node (channel.resolve with channelType:'team'). NEVER repoint these at {{trigger.payload.data.channelId}} (the source/client channel).

CHANNEL BINDING: this only fires meaningfully on a LINKED channel. `external_message.received` carries {{trigger.payload.subjectId}} = the channel's bound client entity (from channels.contextObjectId). On an UNLINKED channel subjectId falls back to the channel id, so the `link-gate` condition (subjectId !== data.channelId) is FALSE and the flow skips. Bind a channel to a client (onboarding, /link-client, or the IS agent's channel.bind on first contact) so subjectId resolves to the entity. NOTE: this is a TWO-PATH comparison — the automation engine's `evaluateCondition` resolves BOTH operands when the right side is a bare context path (trigger./steps./...); it FAILS CLOSED (throws → the run errors) on an unparseable expression, so a malformed gate is loud, not silently taken.

TEAM CHANNEL: resolved at runtime from the client entity — no channel id lives in the template. Requires the client entity to have a sibling `branchPurpose:'team'` channel bound to it (onboarding's channel.ensure/channel.bind creates it) so channel.resolve(channelType:'team') returns one.

GRANT SUBMISSION: `resolve-dossier` (graph.relations, relationType 'submitted_by', direction 'inbound') finds the `grant_submission` entity that `stellar-grant-provision` links onto the client (the client is the TARGET of submitted_by, so the submission is each relation's sourceEntityId). The `submission-found` condition gates the analysis/link/advance on relations.0.sourceEntityId being non-empty, so a client with no submission still gets the flag + review but no orphaned analysis. `advance-submission` and `create-analysis`+`link-analysis` both hang off submission-found's 'yes' handle (decoupled — a proposed/denied analysis write does not block the status advance). REMAINING (noted, not fabricated): to feed the advisor the submission's actual DOCUMENT CONTENT, add a drive/docs read node (e.g. `docs_get`/`drive_get_file`) on the submission's sourceSubmissionUrl once that read verb is confirmed seeded. Until then the advisor receives the submission relations + client id + milestone + message and can web-fetch the doc URL itself.
VERBS: the `resolve-team` + `resolve-dossier` capability nodes reference the seeded `channel.resolve` + `graph.relations` verbs (both work).

AI STEPS (detect/review): both are `capability` nodes running the `ai.generate` builtin verb — a synchronous single-shot LLM completion that calls the IS `/v1/tools/generate` and returns parsed JSON. Each passes `json:'true'`, so the verb's `output` IS the parsed object and it becomes `steps.<id>.output` directly: `detect` returns {reviewNeeded, milestone, reason} (the `gate` condition reads `steps.detect.output.reviewNeeded === true`) and `review` returns {summary} (posted via `steps.review.output.summary`). `ai.generate` is a READ-ONLY builtin (pure compute, no mutation) so it auto-runs inside the automation without spawning a proposal. Message text is interpolated into the prompt by the engine before the verb runs, and fenced as untrusted content IS-side.

RELATION TYPES: reads `submitted_by` (grant_submission -> company) — the SAME relationType `stellar-grant-provision.automation.json` writes via graph.link — and writes `analyzes` (analysis -> grant_submission). Both are grants.yaml entityLinks. Keep provision + review in sync.
ACTIVATION: seeded as `draft`; activate once at least one client channel is bound (client-comms + team) and the dossier relation exists.
